reserveReview.rationale: The configured USDD Data Platform Tron latest-collateral feed capture on 2026-09-04 reports five positive lockedValue categories. Normalizing the current rows (total collateral $1,910,128,975.51) yields TRX 59.9512430832%, Smart Allocator 37.9258008380%, USDT PSM vaults 1.4780536939%, USDT direct vaults 0.0346107749%, and sTRX direct vaults 0.6102916101%. These percentages are the live classification scaffold, not liability shares; TRX includes borrower-owned overcollateralization. Smart Allocator remains an unresolved aggregate because its constituent holdings churn and do not reconcile exactly to reported debt.

reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The 37.9258008380% Smart Allocator live slice is identified as an aggregate protocol position, but its constituent holdings change dynamically and do not reconcile exactly to reported debt; it remains aggregated rather than forcing transient constituent percentages or failure-domain weights.

USDD Smart Allocator live positions and debt

custodyProfile.uncertainty: No third-party custodian exists: reserves sit in USDD protocol contracts (CDP vaults, PSM-USDT vault TSUYvQ5tdd3DijCD1uGunGLpftHuSZ12sQ, and Smart Allocator vaults) whose governance resolves to single-key accounts documented in the mint-authority review. Smart Allocator documentation states the USDD team selects platforms and deploys 'USDD's cash reserve' under team monitoring, so reserve redeployment is discretionary and ongoing; its 2026-08-10 live feed itemizes USDS, USDT, USDT0, and USDC positions across Spark, Aave, JustLend, Morpho, and Venus, but reported debt and deployed holdings do not reconcile exactly at every observation. No trust, SPV, segregation vehicle, or holder claim appears in the Terms of Use or reviewed documentation, so no bankruptcy-remoteness structure is documented. Precedent for unilateral reserve control: roughly 12,000 BTC were removed from collateral in August 2024 without prior DAO approval (existing coin notice). TRX is the subject of the open Clifford et al. v. Tron Foundation et al. class action (SDNY 1:20-cv-2804).
